evidence: Structure (source-verified): tests/scoring.toml, tools/score.py and test.sh are byte-identical to the frozen template (diff empty), so gate/floor/weight policy is template-controlled: gates render/constraints = 0.0 carry no mass (scoring.toml:1-3), score.py:41/47/48 zero the reward on any failed gate or functional <= 0.05 floor, and functional 0.6 outweighs polish 0.2 + visual 0.2 combined, so craft cannot carry more mass than function and a dead app cannot farm polish/visual. Functional weights (scored/functional/judge.toml) sum to 44.0 and follow the stated rule: wall/retention/hold/persistence criteria 4.0, the brief's 'two things matter more than anything else'; ordinary chat 1.5; no criterion over-weights a minor behaviour. Functional floor 0.05 of 44 = 2.2, so no single 1.5/2.0 criterion clears it alone, which is template behaviour, not a task inversion. Gates: render requires only reachability, signed-out privacy, wrong-password refusal and Gwen's sign-in; constraints requires a persisted M-11 post visible to Harriet in a second context - all public requirements (instruction.md; walls-and-retention.md 'staff see every matter'; integration.md persistence), so a stronger app cannot fail a gate a weaker one passes. Inversion probes: (1) cross-criterion state on the shared DB: traced every write in order (gate G1, walls added/lifted, M-13 timer 30->7->off->30, hold release of K-17, deletes) against later preconditions; the 7-day M-13 shortening removes K-13/K-18 only, while later-referenced K-8 (2026-05-10), K-3, K-11 (fixed clock, integration.md) and held K-7 survive, so a correct app's mutations never break a later criterion that a broken app would pass. (2) Conditional legs (timer_changes earlier-versions replay, persistence earlier-versions check, wall_mentions suggestion-request replay, W3 either/or): an app without a version viewer skips a leak check but loses edits_and_stale_edit (3.0); one with a viewer that leaks deleted versions loses timer_changes (4.0) - consistent with the brief's retention priority, not an inversion. edits_and_stale_edit leg 3 passes the current version so a concurrency-checking app is not penalised. Runtime: raw-evidence-index.json scope explicitly states reward discrimination/ranking on these bytes is absent; only previous-v2 hosted ordering exists (Oracle 0.9917 > GPT-5.6 0.8114 > nop 0). Remaining unmeasured inversion mechanism: individual-mode 16 x 550 s + 900 + 900 = 10600 s inside the 11100 s scored timeout (test.sh:224) leaves 500 s for 16 session start-ups; v3 durations are unmeasured (functional judge.toml timeout comment), and a whole-suite timeout zeroes reward, which would hit a fully-correct app (longest sessions) before a fast-failing weak one. Not demonstrated, so not a Fail; risk stays true until a measured ordering/workload run on these bytes exists.
